title: Journalism course and work placements
titleCn: 新闻学课程与政府实习讨论

paragraphs.text: Following instructions from their tutor, you will hear two students called Jeff and Christine discussing their journalism course and their work experience placements in local government.
First, you have some time to look at questions twenty-one to twenty-four.
Now listen carefully and answer questions twenty-one to twenty-four.

Okay, for the next task, I'd like you to work in pairs and review your journalism course and discuss how you think it might be improved. After that, I'd like you to discuss and evaluate the work placement you've just completed.
Okay. Well, Jeff, I'd say we both enjoyed studying about current problems and concerns nationally and locally in the course. That was really well covered.
Right.
I'll tell you what. I really got a lot out of the techniques of writing module, which I managed to apply in our placement. What I took away from that module was how to organize my written work.
That was useful.
But I must admit, when my work colleagues asked me to explain grammar to them, I was hopeless.
[chuckles] I guess I was a bit better at that. I was looking forward to the part of the module on writing summaries, but unfortunately, we never got to that.
But Jeff, you found the module on interviewing techniques particularly useful in the placement, didn't you? Did it help when you were writing press releases for the government?

I never had to conduct interviews for that, but I did have to interview people for the in-house newsletter, so it came in handy there. When the manager asked me to get background information for her, it was always just from written material, though.

Mm-hmm. Let's talk a bit about the module we had on online journalism. Do you think they could add anything to that course to make it better for the placements? I was really disappointed that there wasn't more in the module about how writing materials to be used online differ from, say, newspaper writing in terms of vocabulary, structure, and so on.
That was a shame. I did get a lot out of the practical work we did on dealing with online questions from the public.
And the technical stuff on web design was just about right.

Before we started our placements, the tutor asked us to read the book Government and the Press. I liked it, and since it was published just this year, it was quite current. But it dealt with national affairs and wasn't applicable locally.
I thought it was a good book and practical, but not much help for local government.
No, that's why I didn't use it at all.
Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions twenty-five to thirty.
Now listen and answer questions twenty-five to thirty.
So let's talk about our experience of actually doing the work placement. For example, what did you think of the manager in the public relations department?
Well, she actually didn't seem to know a lot about our journalism course.
Even though she had obviously thought a lot about how to use us best for the placement. But actually, she was extremely busy, and I didn't see much of her.

Me neither. But one of her great strengths seemed to be in getting people to carry out what she asked them to do. Her assistant actually supervised us in our daily activities, and he was brilliant. But the manager had actually been recruited recently from outside, and she didn't know many people in local government or the press.
True.
Now, of all your duties, which did you dislike most?
I found it hard when colleagues asked me to edit their writing.
Yes, it was hard criticizing them. I didn't mind writing policy documents for the manager or articles for the in-house newsletter, which was actually pretty easy.
And I enjoyed going online to look up things for the manager. But when we had to give speeches to students in town, that was agony. I'm always nervous standing in front of an audience.
Oh, me too.
Okay, now our written report of the work placement is due in about ten days. What do you think we need to do to finish it?
Well, we've already put together the government papers to attach to the report, and we've each provided a detailed description of our jobs.
We have to complete the academic bibliography, which I think we've both been putting off.
For sure.
But we finished the recommendations for improving the program. So that leaves the introduction, which we're meeting this week to draft.
And that'll be it.
That is the end of part three. You now have thirty seconds to check your answers to Part three.
